question: In India, the Green Revolution was mainly led by _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**M.S. Swaminathan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Green revolution

 
 
• The green revolution refers to the large increase in the production of food grains resulting from the use of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, especially for wheat and rice crops.
 
• The first phase of the green revolution took place during the period ranging from the mid-1960s up to the mid-1970s.
 
• During the first phase, the use of HYV seeds was restricted to the more affluent states like Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu. 
 
• During the second phase of the green revolution (the mid-1970s to mid-1980s), the HYV technology spread to a larger number of states and benefitted more variety of crops.
 
• The adoption of green revolution technology enabled India to achieve self-sufficiency in the production of food grains.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Facts about the green revolution

 
 
• ​M.S. Swaminathan is known as the father of the green revolution in India.
 
• The green revolution was a great success and changed India’s status from a food-deficient economy to one of the world’s leading agricultural economies.
 
• The green revolution in India started in the year 1965-68 and lasted till the year 1977-78.
 
 

Thus, the green revolution took place in India in the mid-1960s.
